# READ

user or ai harness runs: human serve, to start the reader from anywhere in the project:

cli climbs to the folder that holds human/human.json and gives it to the one human server of the machine:
  a project with no id in human/human.json stops the run, with the reason.
  if a human server already runs on the port, [the project is handed to it](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:give the server the project) and no second server starts; else it starts one.
  a project is handed over from this machine only.
  each project answers under its own id: http://localhost:<port>/<project id>/human/web.html, so one server serves many projects.
  the server [keeps the list of projects](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:read the list of projects) in ~/.human/projects.json; an id it does not know gets no project.
  when the server takes a project, and on the first ask for it, it brings the old maps up to date: a map named explanation_ becomes abstraction_, and an old human/project.json with words becomes a human file named after the project folder.
  the reader comes inside the human program and [is kept in ~/.human](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:from ~/.human/web.html), not in human/ of the project.
  printing the localhost line and the tailnet line.
  a port held by another program, or by an older human server, stops the run and says so.

human init starts the reader too, on its --port: it hands the project to the server that runs, or starts one in the background that writes to human/server/serve.log, and prints the same lines.
  a server that does not answer in about ten seconds stops the run and names that log.
  if the project has no human file yet, human init makes the first one, named after the project folder, and prints its name.

human skills puts the shapes in ~/.human/shapes too.

the installed human program [looks for a new version every hour](compiler/cli/human/updater.py:e1:watch) and gets it ready on its own.
  when one is ready, [a round arrow](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:a lucide icon rotate-ccw) shows at the bottom right of the tree, with the tip "New update, click to reload"; a click on it [restarts the server on the new version](compiler/cli/human/updater.py:e1:restart_when) when no compile or event is open, the arrow turns while it waits, and the page reloads by itself.
  [a human installed from PyPI says](compiler/cli/human/updater.py:e1:from_pypi), at each command, that human moved and how to install it now.

keeps open the conection for the next ask and closes it after 30 seconds with no ask.
  if the browser allows it, sends file info compressed 
     
cli answers human.json with a live file list:
  a deleted file leaves the tree and a new one appears, no init, no restart.
  [human init](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:human init) deletes the map in human/ of a file that is not on disk.
  it keeps the list of files on memorychecks only folders with stamp changed.
  the list carries a version code; the web sends back the code it holds.
  if list didn't change, cli answers no chage. else, answers the whole list.
  a file that did not change since the copy the browser holds gets no chage too, and the browser shows its own copy.
  if the new list comes empty, the page keeps the files it shows.


ai harness leaves a tip for the user's first use: human tip <name> --entry <id> --words <words of one line> --say <words>, kept in human/server/tip.json.
  with --add <new line> --after <words of one line>, the new line goes in a draft of the entry under that line, not compiled, and the tip is on the new line.
  with --draft <words> on a human file or an empty map, the words are kept as a draft that is not compiled, and the human file is made when it does not exist.
  words not found inside one line of the entry, an empty --add, an entry the map does not hold, or a draft on a map that holds an abstraction stops the run.
  human tip --clear takes the tip away.

user opens [the reader](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html): 
  cli sends every map file info in one answer:
    reads the maps .json in human/, reads the file path in each .json, ignores maps with no files and maps that are not good JSON.
    tree doesnt' show human/ folder
  if a tip waits: open the file of the tip.
  a tip on a line unfolds its abstraction, scrolls the line to a third of the screen, lights it with a slow yellow glow and shows the tip under it; a tip on an added line makes the green compile button glow too, and a green hand-drawn arrow with "This is a new change" floats up and down at the right of the line; a draft tip makes the green compile button glow, shows the tip in a box at the top right, and a green hand-drawn arrow with "This is human code" floats at the right of the first line of the draft.
  the tip goes away when you click got it or when that file is compiled.
  the tip shows in a note of dark grey glass with round corners, white words and a dark yellow got it at its right.
  the arrow of a new change, and of human code, is green, bold, in a handwritten font, and takes no click.
  a file shows every abstraction as one folded header, the lowest layer first;
  a click on a pin [jumps to its abstraction](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:jump) or it [switches files](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:#  USER JUMPS TO ANOTHER FILE) 
  a click on a human file pin lands on the abstraction and lights the anchor.
  the back button of the browser brings you to where you were before the jump: the file, the open abstractions and the scroll.
  alt and left, the back button of the mouse and a swipe back on a phone do the same; the forward button, or alt and right, brings you to the next place kept. a writing box left open closes when you go back or forward.
  a pin to a block with no abstraction of its own lands on the abstraction whose anchor names that block and lights the anchor; on a file with no map, it opens the code, scrolls to the lines the pin reaches and lights them a moment.
  each file keeps where you scrolled it: go back to a file and it opens where you left it, a file not read yet opens with its top abstraction unfolded, at the top of the screen.
  the text reads in SF Pro, the San Francisco font of Apple, on every apple device, and in the typewriter font when it is not an apple device.
  the scrollbars of the text, the side one and the vertical one, are small pills with no bar, show only while you scroll, and fade a second after you stop.
  the tree looks like the list of apple notes: the project name sits above in capitals with no card; on a computer the tree fills a soft grey column on the left with no card, #0b0b0b in dark, and the files sit below at the same indent as the project name, and on a phone the files sit in a card with large round corners, dark grey on black in dark, white on soft grey in light, and the open file wears a lighter grey row, with no lively colour.
  on a computer too the reader sits next to the tree with no frame, only a thin faint soft grey line between them, the file name and the count sit centered at the top with no line under them, and the buttons float over the text at the top right, at the height of the file name and the count, the same as on a phone. the text reads at 14px and fades at the top and the bottom there too.
on every screen the compile button sit on the right as an icon in one pill, like of apple notes:
    a filled green play triangle for compile, 
    the save button beside them, a dark yellow circle with a light yellow save icon and no pill, a bit smaller than the pill, pops in on the right of compile while a text is unsaved, far enough from it that compile is not pressed by mistake; 
    the buttons are dark grey glass with a thin lighter edge and white icons, with no lively colour but the green of compile, and the pill goes away when it holds nothing. one tap on the yellow circle saves the draft, as Ctrl+S does.
  on a phone the bar floats over the text: the burger is a round button on the left that opens the tree, and the reader behind it fades dark while the tree is open, and the buttons sit on the right. while you write, the buttons act as they do when you read: they do not go and come back at each character you type, with no staggering, and the screen does not wink when you start to write or when you save. the file name and the count do not show. the text fills the screen with no frame, reads at 14px, keeps that size when you read and when you write, Safari mobile too, and a long line scrolls sideways. the scrollbars do not show; when a line is wider than the screen, a thin pill as far down the screen as it goes shows where you are in it while you scroll, and a drag on that pill scrolls the text sideways. the text fades at the top and the bottom, with no frame. dark is a pure black ground with off-white words, like apple notes, and light a pure white ground with near-black words. the colour of the reader fills the whole screen, the phone's own top bar takes the page's colour, light or dark, and the page does not zoom.


# SYNCRONIZATION

user changes the code
user or ai harness run human sync <name>
  a folder in the place of the name is refused.
  
cli runs [a deterministic pass](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:cmd_sync):
  [maps every old line to its new line](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the line map),
  [re-resolves every pin and every span](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the re-resolving).
  if only lines moved, return.
cli finds the abstractions the change touches: lines changed, a pin broken, new lines inside the block.
if the user wrote the words first and the code was written for them: human sync <name> --for <id>. that abstraction [leaves the list](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the entry that leaves): its spans and pins follow the code and no word changes, unless its block is gone. an id no abstraction carries stops the run. a stale repair takes no --for.
cli writes instruction to ai compiler: 
  the file and its absolute path — read the whole file —, 
  the diff,
  [the project files it imports](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the line about the neighbours),
  the blocks,
  the abstractions to mend,
  the rules:
    keep the untouched lines, 
    keep every anchor, 
    add a sentence for each behaviour the change added.
    an abstraction of your own words goes in [named as yours](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the mark on your words),
    find the smallest edit, in the user's voice.

ai compiler [answers with the mended texts](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:ask_claude), 
runs at the project root,
runs claude opus 5.5 at medium effort,
the instruction given through the pipe and never on the command line, so a long one is not cut short.
if claude fails, cli stops and says the reason claude gave.

cli [gates the answer on a copy](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the rebuild), 
tries up to --tries times. checks if: 
  every block exists,
  every anchor kept, 
  every needed word alive. 
  four failures leave the map untouched.
  
the map gets saved; 
the abstractions that point into a mended one get marked stale:
  in the file's map,
  in every map with no code under it, when one of its abstractions pins the mended one if a word changed, and not if the pins alone moved.
           
shows warning:
  if [new lines landed inside an entry](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the pieces the new lines fall in) and no word changed.
  if [the sync moved words of your own](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the word when your words moved):
the first copy stays in the map, human show marks the entry with [the line that brings them back](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the word about your words).

if user wants to sync the whole project or a human file, [human sync <bare name>](compiler/cli/human/cmd_project.py:e1:cmd_sync). which uses the old state: git HEAD;

cli asks git for [the files that changed](compiler/cli/human/cmd_project.py:e1:changed_files),
re-resolves the file, block, and abstraction pins, and names each one that broke,
[sends one instruction](compiler/cli/human/cmd_project.py:e1:cmd_sync) for the abstraction that pin a changed file.
the diff holds only the changed files those abstractions pin. a file git does not hold yet has no old copy: the diff shows only the lines the pins reach, as new lines.
           
a human file abstraction with the user words goes in named as the users' there too.
the same warning follows when the answer moved them.
--for is taken here too: the abstraction it names leaves the list unless one of its pins broke, its pins follow the code and its words stay. an id no abstraction carries stops the run, and --for with --stale is refused.


# A PARENT ABSTRACTION CHANGED

if abstraction 1 changed by a sync or a retext and a second abstraction points into it:
  abstraction 2 gets [marked as stale](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:mark_children) and a copy of the old text gets added to its json file.
           
the mark is a list. a second changed parent adds [a note of its own](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:add_note),
if parent changes twice before the repair then keeps its first old text. the versions between are the base of nothing. 
if abstraction 2 retexts it still keeps the mark; 
only if repair the mark gets off. which lets the tool know the mending happened and was not guessed.

user asks for the repair: human sync <name> --stale 2

cli writes the second letter: one page for each changed parent.
  its old text, 
  its new text, 
  the diff between the two
  then the dependent's text,
  the rules: mend the words that went wrong, 
  keep every anchor and [every word another entry needs](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:needed_words),
  carry a new fact down at the dependent's own level, pinned at the parent's new anchor.
if the dependent holds the user's words, the letter asks for the smallest edit, in the user's voice.
a parent that is gone stops the run.

ai harness answers with the mended dependent. words only, never code.

cli [gates and saves](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:repair_stale); 
marks the dependents of entry 2 as stale in turn.
a repair that moved words of your own is named on the spot, as a sync's is.
a parent's child can be a parent: the next abstraction layer waits for the users next word, one layer at a time. the layers cross maps too. a human file can be the parent of a human file. the chain never turns back on itself.
a human file abstraction made stale by a file's abstraction is repaired the same way:
    each note naming the map and the abstraction it waits on, with the parent read from that map: [human sync <human file> --stale](compiler/cli/human/cmd_project.py:e1:repair_stale).



# EDITOR ON READER

user clicks the text of an entry: a box opens in its place, the raw text, pins and all. the same text retext takes — with the caret where you clicked, and it grows as you type and reaches down to the bottom of the screen.
the box grows until its last line shows whole, also when a line wider than the screen gives it a sideways scroll bar.
tab puts four spaces, or moves the selected lines four spaces right; shift+tab moves them back.
the caret is yellow and slightly thick, the colour of the dot in the tree, and the words you select light yellow too.
the caret stays right after the last letter on a line of any length.
a file with no map shows one place for its telling and the code of the file under it, in the colours of its language, light or dark as the page, and the bar says there is no abstraction yet; 
an empty map with no code under it offers a new abstraction, and once a map holds an entry that place is gone. 
escape, or a click away, closes the box and keeps what you wrote — only the box now open answers a click away;
a click on a pin jumps and opens no box. 
a pin you just typed, one the map does not hold yet, [is read from the target it names](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:guessAnchor).
a pin the page cannot follow shows that target beside the words, and the caret counts past the shown name, so a click after such a pin still lands where you clicked.
typing keeps nothing
if Ctrl+S or the yellow circle put the draft in the server:
  human/server/drafts.json, so another browser or the phone opens the same drafts.
  the yellow circle stays until you press it.
  if the server does not answer, the draft stays in the box and the bar asks if human serve is running.
  an empty draft, or one that the map or the file already holds, is thrown away.
  drafts an older page kept in the browser move to the server the next time the page opens.
every file that holds a writing the map does not hold yet [carries a small yellow dot in its row of the tree](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:markWaiting), the ones you are not reading too, and the dot goes out when the writing lands.
your words [stay in the place you wrote them](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:keepBox) when the page draws again between one box and the next.
the page keeps its place through all of it: the box opens, grows and closes where you were reading, and an empty place for a telling lights under the pointer, so you see it can be written in.

user makes a file from the page
a right-click on the tree gives the two of them, create file and create human, and the box opens under the row you clicked; the empty space under the rows takes the folder of the last row above it.
if create file:
  a right-click on a folder, or on a file, puts the name you type inside that folder
  the box opens empty and holds the folder of the row out of sight, so you type the name alone and it lands in that folder; 
    a name that starts with / lands at the root
  [the server makes the file empty](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:the new file), so it opens on its new abstraction.
  the code comes under your words. 
if create human:
  [the right-click list takes a bare name](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e2:the human file).
  refuse if bare name is already held by another human file or a file at the root
  the folder you right-clicked is kept in the map, so the name stands in the tree under that folder as <name>.human, while its record stays human/human_<name>.json.
  the map opens on its new abstraction with no file under it.
no event is queued.
a path out of the project, into human/, or onto a file already there is refused, with the reason. 
the tree follows the files on disk.
git holds no old copy of a file made here,so its first sync runs against an empty old version.

user asks for an abstraction the user did not write himself, by three roads: on a file with no map the open
           place carries a decompile button — not on an empty file, whose words come first — and one
           click asks claude for the whole-file telling;
           on a mapped entry you highlight words and right-click for expand abstraction, which opens a
           write place on top whose head is the button — your words there, or none at all; a right-click
           on the head of an entry gives create abstraction, a plainer telling over that entry, nothing
           to write. These three send themselves at the click and wait for no compile button, and each
           opens from [the little menu of a right click](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:the menu).
           An expansion is a deeper telling of the words you highlighted: it stands above the entry,
           and the entry pins those words down into it, as a zoom on one block stands above the
           telling of the whole file.
user takes an abstraction away: the same right-click on its head offers delete abstraction, and
           [the head turns into the button](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:to take that one away), with a cancel beside it.
           One click takes the entry out at once — this road waits for no compile button and queues
           no event, because nothing is left for claude to do.
  
cli, it runs human undo <name> --entry <id>, and [the gate refuses it](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the gate)
           while another abstraction stands on that abstraction.
           [The training store](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the training store) and its open session take no part in the undo any more.
  
user presses the compile button, which stands in the bar while a text differs from the map:
           [it sends every place you changed](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:#  USER PRESSES COMPILE AND SERVER ANSWERS), one after the other. The map changes only then.
           while the page waits for the server, no words show on top and the compile button turns faint and takes no press.
  
server takes request [as JSON](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:as JSON) —
           and [runs the command you would have typed](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:e1:the command run), one per changed text,
           with the built human program itself, or with human through python:
           an entry rewritten goes in as human retext <name> <id> --verbatim, a first telling as
           human map <name> --verbatim, and code on a file with no map is written to the file.
           A map that holds no entries counts as no map here.
           An expansion you wrote words for goes in the same way, as human map <name> --verbatim, so the
           map holds your words before claude works; an expansion with no words, a decompile and a
           create map nothing at the click — the event alone waits.
           A file under human/ is refused — the maps take no writing.
           The gates are the ones of flow 1: a refusal comes back to the page in the command's own
           words, named by the file and the place it came from, and nothing is queued.

one event appended to human/server/events.jsonl: the kind, the name, the paths of the map and
           the file, the entry, the old text and the new, and for a code write
           [the pins that reach the file](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:e1:the pins that reach a file).
           An expansion and a create name the entry they stand on, and an expansion carries the
           highlighted words with their pins.

user arms the listening once, from the project root: human watch, with no pipeline to filter.

cli [prints every event claude has not finished](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:e1:cmd_watch), one JSON line each, then
           follows the queue; --once prints what waits now and returns. An event printed in an earlier
           session comes back marked replay, so claude reads the maps before it syncs anything.

ai harness takes them in order, by [the writing part of the human skill](compiler/cli/human/skills/human/SKILL.md:The reader writes):
           reads the diff of your words, writes the code they ask for — in a new file when no file of the
           project holds that thing —, removes the code they no longer ask for, syncs every map that stood on
           them with --for, so your words follow the code and no word of them changes, and pins the new sentences back in. A decompile, a create, or an expansion with no
           words has no text of yours to read: claude writes that telling itself, in the shape the catalog gives the file, and maps it.
           Then [human ack <number>](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:e1:cmd_ack) — the queue
           advances and says how many are left.

user sees the wait in the page: the entry is marked compiling until the ack, because the reader
           [asks every three seconds](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:pollQueue) and the door answers with
           [what still waits](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:e1:pending). When the wait ends, the page reads
           that map again, so the new words show.

user or ai harness run human sync <name>
  
cli runs a deterministic pass:
  maps every old line to its new line,
  re-resolves every pin and every span.
  if only lines moved, return.
cli finds the abstractions the change touches: lines changed, a pin broken, new lines inside the block.
if the user wrote the words first and the code was written for them: human sync <name> --for <id>. that abstraction leaves the list: its spans and pins follow the code and no word changes, unless its block is gone. an id no abstraction carries stops the run. a stale repair takes no --for.
cli writes instruction to ai compiler: 
  the file and its absolute path — read the whole file —, 
  the diff,
  the project files it imports,
  the blocks,
  the abstractions to mend,
  the rules:
    keep the untouched lines, 
    keep every anchor, 
    add a sentence for each behaviour the change added.
    an abstraction of your own words goes in named as yours,
    find the smallest edit, in the user's voice.

ai compiler answers with the mended texts, 
runs at the project root,
runs claude opus 5.5 at medium effort,
the instruction given through the pipe and never on the command line, so a long one is not cut short.
if claude fails, cli stops and says the reason claude gave.

cli gates the answer on a copy, 
tries up to --tries times. checks if: 
  every block exists,
  every anchor kept, 
  every needed word alive. 
  four failures leave the map untouched.
  
the map gets saved; 
the abstractions that point into a mended one get marked stale:
  in the file's map,
  in every map with no code under it, when one of its abstractions pins the mended one if a word changed, and not if the pins alone moved.
           
shows warning:

the first copy stays in the map, human show marks the entry with the line that brings them back.

sends one instruction for the abstraction that pin a changed file.
the diff holds only the changed files those abstractions pin. a file git does not hold yet has no old copy: the diff shows only the lines the pins reach, as new lines.
           
a project abstraction with the user words goes in named as the users' there too.
the same warning follows when the answer moved them.
--for is taken here too: the abstraction it names leaves the list unless one of its pins broke, its pins follow the code and its words stay. an id no abstraction carries stops the run, and --for with --stale is refused.

if abstraction 1 changed by a sync or a retext and a second abstraction points into it:
  abstraction 2 gets marked as stale and a copy of the old text gets added to its json file.
           
the mark is a list. a second changed parent adds a note of its own,
if parent changes twice before the repair then keeps its first old text. the versions between are the base of nothing. 
if abstraction 2 retexts it still keeps the mark; 
only if repair the mark gets off. which lets the tool know the mending happened and was not guessed.

  its old text,

  then the dependent's text,
  the rules: mend the words that went wrong,

  carry a new fact down at the dependent's own level, pinned at the parent's new anchor.

a parent that is gone stops the run.

cli gates and saves; 
marks the dependents of entry 2 as stale in turn.
a repair that moved words of your own is named on the spot, as a sync's is.
a parent's child can be a parent: the next abstraction layer waits for the users next word, one layer at a time. the layers cross maps too. a human file can be the parent of a human file. the chain never turns back on itself.
